episodes.183235: Scattered thunderstorms developed along and ahead of a cold front during the late afternoon into the mid evening hours.  A few of these became strong to severe, with damaging wind and isolated hail.
episodes.183270: A disorganized cluster of storms pushed northeastward from far southwestern Pennsylvania into and across central Pennsylvania during the afternoon and early evening hours of September 7, 2023. The individual cells intensified and eventually merged into a north-south line that crossed the Susquehanna Valley. Wind damage was the primary impact, although one severe hail report was received.
episodes.183461: An approaching mid-upper level trough from the TN Valley provided sufficient synoptic forcing across eastern GA for widespread severe pulse convection. Ample low level moisture and steepening lapse rates as the trough neared allowed for strong instability to develop, with very weak deep and low level wind shear. A deep layer of mid-level dry air wrapped around the trough aloft and provided sufficient evaporative cooling aloft for both severe hail production and enhanced downbursts.
episodes.183467: An approaching mid-upper level trough from the TN Valley provided sufficient synoptic forcing across South Carolina for widespread severe pulse convection. Ample low level moisture and steepening lapse rates as the trough neared allowed for strong instability to develop, with very weak deep and low level wind shear. A deep layer of mid-level dry air wrapped around the trough aloft and provided sufficient evaporative cooling aloft for both severe hail production and enhanced downbursts.
episodes.183717: A few isolated severe thunderstorms developed as a result of terrain circulations after several days of late season heat.
episodes.183718: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed along a lee pressure trough after several days of late season heat. Several of these storms turned severe, producing both damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.183721: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed along a lee pressure trough after several days of late season heat. Several of these storms turned severe, producing both damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.183725: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed along a lee pressure trough after several days of late season heat. Several of these storms turned severe, producing both damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.183740: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed along a lee pressure trough after several days of late season heat. Several of these storms produced strong winds and hail over the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.183909: An advancing cold front coupled with afternoon heating brought scattered thunderstorms that just clipped northeastern Tennessee. Large hail and brief damaging winds occurred with the storms.
episodes.184152: A surface boundary moved through Central New York, kicking off a line of storms across the region. This line of thunderstorms had two portions with one line moving north and another line moving east. With a moisture rich and unstable environment ahead of the boundary, thunderstorms quickly became severe. Damaging wind gusts were the main threat with these storms. The majority of damage reports were for downed trees and utility lines.
episodes.184153: A surface boundary moved through Northeast Pennsylvania, kicking off a line of storms that crossed the region. There were some scattered thunderstorm cells that did pop up ahead of this main line of storms which moved north and east across the area during the mid-to-late afternoon. With a moisture rich and unstable environment ahead of the boundary, thunderstorms quickly became severe. Damaging wind gusts were the main threat with these storms. The majority of damage reports were for downed trees and utility lines. Unfortunately, there was one fatality in Susquehanna County due to a falling tree that landed on a man.
episodes.184237: Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms developed during the afternoon with isolated damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184238: An active period of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms resulted in several reports of wind damage.  Most of the damage occurred on September 7th as a cluster of severe storms moved through Tallahassee.  In addition, a significant downburst with winds estimated around 85 mph occurred near Spring Creek in Wakulla county.
episodes.184464: On September 6th, a cold front entered into West Virginia and stirred up showers and thunderstorms for the afternoon. One storm in particular that passed through Fayette County was strong enough to cause two trees and power lines to be blown down. The severe threat quickly diminished as drier air filtered in behind the frontal passage.||Another weak cold front arrived two days later on the 8th, this time imposing a flash flooding threat. Despite the front having already crossed much of West Virginia by the afternoon, there was still enough lift along the foothills and mountains that promoted slow moving showers and storms. Enough rain fell in McDowell County that resulted in high water along a local road for a few hours.
episodes.184852: An isolated severe storm generated half dollar sized hail 7 miles southeast of Hayes in Stanley county.
episodes.184875: An isolated thunderstorm that formed on the northern edge of an outflow boundary over central Lake Ontario tracked east late in the evening producing prolific lightning out over the lake. This storm reached Jefferson County shortly before midnight and produced isolated wind damage before weakening as it moved farther inland away from Lake Ontario.
episodes.184876: Out ahead of a cold front during the last very warm and humid day of a recent stretch of hot weather, thunderstorms developed mid to late afternoon from central Pennsylvania to central New York. A line of severe storms developed in this area and lifted north across the Finger Lakes and eventually the eastern Lake Ontario region. Several reports of wind damage were received as these storms moved through, especially over Oswego and Lewis counties.
episodes.185105: Non-severe thunderstorms tracked across Allegheny County during the evening of September 7th.  Localized 3-hour rainfall totals of 1.5 to 2.5 inches north of Pittsburgh created some localized flash flooding issues.
episodes.185149: An upper level disturbance and cold front moved across a moderately unstable airmass due to near record warmth across northern NY. Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon, some of which produced locally damaging winds.
episodes.185150: An upper level disturbance and cold front moved across a moderately unstable airmass due to near record warmth across VT. Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon, some of which produced locally damaging winds.
episodes.185613: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over eastern Lenawee county.
episodes.185620: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.185638: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the Pine Ridge of South Dakota during the early evening hours of September 7th. As this isolated thunderstorm activity tracked to the east-southeast, thunderstorm coverage increased over north central Nebraska. Some storms were severe with hail up to half dollar size and wind gusts up to 60 MPH.
episodes.185641: A lee trough east of the North Carolina Appalachians amid a warm and moist atmosphere led to the development of widely isolated showers and storms over the central North Carolina Piedmont in the evening hours. A few storms produced quarter-size hail and damaging winds over Stanly, Anson, and Granville Counties.
episodes.185719: Diurnal instability with unseasonable late season heat and humidity supported afternoon thunderstorm development. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds in southeast Aroostook county.
episodes.185759: A frontal boundary and low pressure system located to the west and east of eastern New York was the focus for rounds of showers and thunderstorms each day September 7-9. Strong to severe thunderstorms were more widespread on September 7-8. These storms resulted in numerous reports of tree and powerline damage, as well as thousands without power and several road closures.
episodes.185794: A cold front and upper trough slowly approached the area on September 7th, providing a source of lift for the pre-existing instability generated by diurnal heating across southern and central Virginia. This combination created an atmosphere that was conducive for damaging winds gusts. Around 2900 people were left without power in Roanoke, and another 655 were without power in Henry County.
episodes.185802: A cold front and upper trough slowly approached the area on September 7th, providing a source of lift for the pre-existing instability generated by diurnal heating across northwest North Carolina. This combination created an atmosphere that was conducive for damaging winds gusts.
episodes.185811: A weak surface trough moved into the area. This feature moved into a very unstable airmass as it was a hot and humid day. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed, producing large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185812: A weak surface trough moved into the area. This feature moved into a very unstable airmass as it was a hot and humid day. Strong to severe thunderstorms developed, producing large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185838: A line of severe thunderstorms developed to the west of the area along a surface trough in an unstable environment characterized by SBCAPE values of 2500 to 2500 J/kg. These thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts across southeast NY.
episodes.185861: A cold front pushed across north Mississippi during the late afternoon and early evening hours on September 6, 2023.  Thunderstorms initially developed along and south of Interstate 40 as the airmass became unstable and wind shear aloft increased due|to a mid-level jet maximum approaching the region. Thunderstorms became more numerous as the front pushed into north Mississippi, eventually forming a line with several reports of damaging wind and a few occurrences of large hail.
episodes.185974: A cluster of thunderstorms shifted from Southern Arkansas into Northern Louisiana on September 7th, advancing along a weak cold front situated near the Arkansas/Louisiana state line. Near the surface cold front, temperatures surged into the mid and upper 90s, with dewpoints near 70F, yielding moderate MLCAPE values of 2000-2500 J/kg. Given the moist environment, there was an increasing potential from damaging gusts due to strong downdrafts. In addition, the modest deep-layer shear resulted in thunderstorm clustering, and these clusters were the preferred locations for isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts with a few damage reports from Bienville and Red River Parishes.
episodes.185985: A weakening frontal system moved southeast into an unstable airmass over Central GA. Steep lapse rates and instability meant scattered thunderstorms over Central and East-Central GA developed damaging winds and some hail.
episodes.186123: A pair of shortwaves moved across central and south central Louisiana during the afternoons of the 7th and 8th. While only a couple thunderstorms occurred on the 7th, a southward traveling line of severe weather developed on the second day.
episodes.186162: Thunderstorms triggered off of a convergent boundary during peak heating across southeast Mississippi and propagated southwestward across coastal Mississippi and southeast Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours. Fueled by high instability and drier mid-level air, these storms quickly became severe and produced damaging winds in their path. The complex eventually made its way over the coastal waters where it finally dissipated.
episodes.186163: Thunderstorms triggered off of a convergent boundary during peak heating across southeast Mississippi and propagated southwestward across coastal Mississippi and southeast Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours. Fueled by high instability and drier mid-level air, these storms quickly became severe and produced damaging winds in their path. The complex eventually made its way over the coastal waters where it finally dissipated.
episodes.186164: Thunderstorms triggered off of a convergent boundary during peak heating across southeast Mississippi and propagated southwestward across coastal Mississippi and southeast Louisiana during the afternoon and evening hours. Fueled by high instability and drier mid-level air, these storms quickly became severe and produced damaging winds in their path. The complex eventually made its way over the coastal waters where it finally dissipated.
episodes.186171: A disturbance in northwest flow aloft triggered a round of severe thunderstorms as it interacted with a hot and unstable air mass over southeast Arkansas and northern Mississippi. These thunderstorms produced some wind damage and hail as they moved across northern and central Mississippi.
episodes.186202: An anomalously warm and humid airmass was in place across the state of New Hampshire on September 7th with high temperatures well into the 80s along with surface moisture.  This allowed for high instability values to develop through the day.  A weak frontal boundary began  to approach Western new Hampshire by the evening where a few lines of thunderstorms developed and slowly moved into the Connecticut River Valley.  A few isolated storms became severe with large hail and damaging winds, but overall the damage was sporadic and mostly confided near the Vermont border near the Connecticut River Valley.
episodes.186241: Isolated thunderstorms along with a couple of storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina throughout the late afternoon and evening. Several of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts and/or large hail.
episodes.186242: Widely scattered thunderstorms along with a couple of storm clusters developed over western North Carolina, mainly during the evening. Several of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts and/or large hail.
episodes.186246: A disturbance in northwest flow aloft triggered a round of severe thunderstorms as it interacted with a hot and unstable air mass over portions of southern Mississippi.
episodes.186248: A disturbance in northwest flow aloft triggered a round of severe thunderstorms as it interacted with a hot and unstable air mass over portions of Northeast and Central Louisiana.
